title: The Art & Science of Benchmarking Agents — Vincent Chen, Snorkel AI
talk_summary: Vincent Chen presents a framework for building effective agent benchmarks: rigorous task validation, distributional diversity, model headroom, and robust multi-dimensional eval methodology, plus differentiators like thesis, roadmap, and researcher UX. He argues benchmarks should model real-world environment complexity, autonomy horizon, and output complexity to close the evaluation gap.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define a taxonomy of real-world tasks and rare but high-impact failure modes, then intentionally distribute eval cases across it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: define a clear taxonomy for the domain, for real-world tasks, and distribute those tasks uh intentionally

takeaways.what_they_do: Use an original author, independent reviewers, and adjudicators with revision opportunities; payouts depend on reviewer agreement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: multi-reviewer protocol where there was an original author, you know, there were there were reviewers and adjudicators in the loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure cost, latency, reasoning traces, tool use, and policy constraints in addition to task accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: go beyond accuracy to capture real-world dimensions that matter, right? This is everything from cost, latency

takeaways.technique: Modular eval harness with easy contribution
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide a standardized harness that makes it simple to run models/agents against the benchmark and simple to add new tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: really simple to run models and agents against your benchmark. It's really simple to contribute new tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep benchmark tasks that expose real capability soft spots and reliably separate frontier models, rather than saturating at high scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: benchmark is unsaturated that it exposes real soft spots in capabilities and reliably separates where models sit
takeaways.numbers: ARC-AGI 3: frontier models under 1% at launch

takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmark agents in environments with org-specific policies, Slack context, screenshots, flaky toolchains, distributed CI, and human reviewer preferences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A real codebase has org-specific policies, you know, lots of Slack context, uh screenshots, flaky toolchains
